proposal_title: Security Credential Injection, Buffer Zeroing & Telemetry Redaction
domain_specific_rationale: CP-007 eliminates fictional, unverified claims of a hardware SecretEnclave and replaces them with an implementable, defense-in-depth security model. It mandates OS/Vault runtime secret injection at process startup (disallowing hardcoded credentials), in-memory credential management with explicit Node.js buffer wiping (buf.fill(0)) to prevent memory scraping from GC heap dumps, and automatic redaction of Authorization, Cookie, set-cookie, and bearer tokens across traces, logs, and metrics via R14 Observability SDK. It also formalizes chmod 700 protection on Chrome user data directories and OS-pipe Native Messaging isolation. This is essential for protecting Google/browser session material and provider API keys across execution boundaries.
evidence_citations: 04_integration/SECURITY_MODEL.md:Lines 7-18 (Trust Boundaries 1-4: VPC isolation, worker chmod 700, in-memory buf.fill(0), telemetry redaction)
capability_impact: Directly implements and hardens CAP-07 (Security & Isolation). Establishes clear trust boundaries separating core workflow services from privileged local execution zones without degrading video generation throughput.
residual_risk: Node.js string conversions of secrets may leave immutable, unmanaged string copies in V8 heap memory before buffer zeroing occurs. Mitigation: R07 Provider SDK and R09 Browser Worker must enforce handling tokens strictly as raw Uint8Array/Buffer instances without intermediate UTF-8 string casting. CI suites must enforce automated memory leakage and redaction regression tests.
